analysis:
I examined PromptTokenCache.swift (new), the ProviderPromptContractPipeline.tokenize change, and the InboundDecode refactor.

PromptTokenCache: a SHA-256 key over a domain tag, the length-prefixed scope and the piece bytes partitions the cache by scope. The store is bounded (default 32 MiB, max 4 GiB by env) and evicts in two generations; oversized pieces are not admitted. Encoding fans out to at most 4 workers. The splitter declines for lstrip/rstrip tokens, overlapping added tokens, or non-identity post-processors. A load-time self-check and sampled background re-verification (first 4 prompts, then 1 in 256) disable the cache on any token mismatch. I found no correctness-based poisoning path. Cached data is token IDs of prompt text already held in process memory, so no new plaintext persistence beyond the existing process-memory exposure (T-011/T-014). The background verification task retains the messages briefly in memory. DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 kills it. The one gap is the TTL-less same-scope timing oracle in the finding (T-041/SEC-035).

Pipeline: the cache path is used only when promptCacheScope is non-nil and the tokenizer conforms to PromptTokenCaching. Neither the callers that derive the scope nor the conformance were supplied. Next pass should confirm the scope comes from the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, that nil or empty scope falls back to the unchanged path, and that standalone mode cannot share a single scope across tenants.

InboundDecode: this is a refactor that merges five parses into one. Repair and normalization are unchanged. Extensions are still taken from the original bytes, and each field is decoded independently. The GLM raw-control validation depends on modelType, which decodeInboundChatRequest does not pass, so it defaults to nil like the old default. Whether the old admission callers passed a modelType is not visible; this needs a check in the integration pass that the GLM validation path was not skipped.

findings.detail: PromptPieceTokenStore keeps scoped piece token IDs in RAM with no TTL, only a byte-bounded two-generation eviction. A cached prefix saves roughly 0.1-0.35 s of tokenization for 27-46K-token prompts, a much larger signal than a KV hit. Within one cache scope a caller can probe whether a known prefix was recently submitted. The signal can outlive the 30-minute sliding TTL that T-041 and SEC-035 assume for prefix reuse. It lasts until eviction or tokenizer unload, and it applies even when the KV prefix cache declines a donation (adoption, benefit, endurance or disk guards). Cross-account leakage is prevented by the scope-keyed SHA-256, assuming the coordinator authors the scope. The T-041 and SEC-035 acceptance does not cover this second oracle. Fix: add a TTL to the piece store matching the prefix-cache TTL, or record this oracle explicitly in T-041 and SEC-035. The scope must stay coordinator-derived, and nil or empty scopes must take the unchanged path.
findings.title: Prompt-token cache adds a same-scope tokenization timing oracle outside T-041's 30-minute TTL bound
